facts.statement: The species was originally named Ogmodirus martini by Williston and Moodie in 1913, though the specific name was later emended to martinii.
facts.quote: KUVP 441 was named as Ogmodirus martini by Williston & Moodie (1913) and the specific name was emended to martinii by Moodie (1916), but the original name takes precedence.

facts.statement: A second species, Ogmodirus ischiadicus, was initially placed in its own genus but has since been referred to Styxosaurus.
facts.quote: A second species, Ogmodirus ischiadicus (based on specimen KUVP 434), was initially placed within its own genus, Thalassiosaurus, and has since been referred to Styxosaurus.

facts.statement: Welles (1962) suggested Ogmodirus may belong to the Elasmosauridae, but noted the genus is dubious beyond the suborder Plesiosauria due to fossil condition.
facts.quote: According to Welles (1962), Ogmodirus martini may be member of the Elasmosauridae, a group of marine animals related to Elasmosaurus, but the condition of the fossils discovered to date means the genus is dubious beyond Plesiosauria.

facts.statement: Sepkoski (2002) assigned Ogmodirus to the Plesiosauria without a more specific classification.
facts.quote: Sepkoski (2002) asignó a Ogmodirus a Plesiosauria, sin asignación más específica.

facts.statement: Ogmodirus lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: Ogmodirus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur characterized by an extremely long neck that lived during the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Ogmodirus es un género extinto de plesiosaurio con un cuello extremadamente largo que vivió en el Cretácico.

rejected.statement: Ogmodirus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur found in the Late Cretaceous Greenhorn Limestone of Kansas.
rejected.quote: Ogmodirus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur found in the Cenomanian-Turonian (Late Cretaceous) Greenhorn Limestone of Kansas.
